**Sitmar Cruises** and its predecessor **Sitmar Line** were company names derived from the acronym for the **Società Italiana Trasporti Marittimi** (English: Italian Maritime Transport Company). SITMAR originally was an Italian shipping line founded by Russian émigré Alexandre Vlasov, however the company's headquarters were later transferred to <Monaco>. Vlasov initially operated cargo services from 1937, gradually replacing these with passenger services from 1947 until 1988, when SITMAR was sold to the [Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company](P%26O_(company) "P&O (company)") (P&O). After the sale, most of the former SITMAR ships were transferred to the fleet of P&O subsidiary [Princess Cruises](Princess_Cruises "Princess Cruises"), while one, [TSS *Fairstar*](TSS_Fairstar "TSS Fairstar"), became the sole vessel of the newly created P&O-Sitmar Cruises (later P&O Holidays). As of July 2018, one briefly named former SITMAR ship (*Sitmar Fair Majesty*) was still operational, as [Cruise & Maritime Voyages](Cruise_%26_Maritime_Voyages "Cruise & Maritime Voyages")'s [*Columbus*](MV_Columbus "MV Columbus").[[1]](Sitmar_Cruises#cite_note-1)[[2]](Sitmar_Cruises#cite_note-2) However, two other vessels originally ordered by SITMAR but delivered to P&O, sailed under the Princess banner before operating from Australia for a number of years, such as *[Pacific Jewel](Karnika "Karnika")* and *[Pacific Dawn](Pacific_Dawn "Pacific Dawn")*. As of 2021, *Pacific Dawn*, set to become *Ambience* is the only survivor, with *Columbus* and *Pacific Jewel* being sold for scrap.

## Company history

SITMAR began when Alexandre Vlasov carried coal in the Mediterranean, using two small cargo ships. During the [Second World War](Second_World_War "Second World War"), these ships were lost to the company. Vlasov restarted SITMAR after the war and slowly assembled a new fleet of passenger and cargo ships. SITMAR obtained contracts with the [International Refugee Organisation](International_Refugee_Organisation "International Refugee Organisation") (IRO) to take refugees from <Europe> to <Australia> and other nations.

SITMAR's first vessel to operate services to Australia was the Castelbianco. Amongst the many companies contracted to carry displaced people, SITMAR's vessels were noted for providing higher quality accommodation and food.

During the 1950s, SITMAR became a major passenger shipping company. It offered regular services between Europe and Australia for migrants and full-fare paying passengers. For several years, the company operated voyages between <Europe>, [Central America](Central_America "Central America") and [South America](South_America "South America"). Periodically SITMAR also engaged in the seasonal tourist trade between <Europe>, the [United States](United_States "United States") and <Canada>.

The Central and South America services, also the North Atlantic summer services, were abandoned by 1957. **P&O** (in full,  **The Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company**[[1]](P%26O#cite_note-1)) was a British [shipping](Shipping "Shipping") and [logistics](Logistics "Logistics") company dating from the early 19th century. Formerly a [public company](Public_company "Public company"), it was sold to [DP World](DP_World "DP World") in March 2006 for £3.9 billion. DP World currently operate several P&O branded businesses, [P&O Ferries](P%26O_Ferries "P&O Ferries"), [Istithmar P&O Estates](Istithmar_World "Istithmar World"), and [P&O Maritime Logistics](P%26O_Maritime_Logistics "P&O Maritime Logistics"). It also operates P&O Heritage, which is the official historic archive and collection of P&O.

[P&O Cruises](P%26O_Cruises "P&O Cruises") was sold in 2000, and is now owned and operated by [Carnival Corporation & plc](Carnival_Corporation_%26_plc "Carnival Corporation & plc"), although the trademark for "P&O Cruises" is still held by the Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company and used under licence.[[2]](P%26O#cite_note-2) The former shipping business, [P&O Nedlloyd](P%26O_Nedlloyd "P&O Nedlloyd"), was bought by and is now part of [Maersk Line](Maersk_Line "Maersk Line").

## History

**Home Lines** was an Italian passenger [shipping company](Shipping_company "Shipping company") that operated both [ocean liners](Ocean_liners "Ocean liners") and [cruise ships](Cruise_ships "Cruise ships"). The company was founded in 1946, and it ceased operations in 1988 when merged into [Holland America Line](Holland_America_Line "Holland America Line"). Although based in <Genoa>, Home Lines was an international company with ships registered in <Panama>, while the original company chairman Eugen Eugenides was [Greek](Greeks "Greeks"). By the time Home Lines was merged into Holland America, they were one of the most highly regarded cruise lines in the world.[[2]](Home_Lines#cite_note-simplon-2)

Home Lines were connected to [Cosulich Lines](Cosulich_Line "Cosulich Line"), [Swedish American Line](Swedish_American_Line "Swedish American Line") and [Hamburg-America Line](Hamburg-America_Line "Hamburg-America Line"). Eugen Eugenides' adopted son Nicolaos Vernicos-Eugenides cofounded the [Hamburg Atlantic Line](Hamburg_Atlantic_Line "Hamburg Atlantic Line") in 1958, and he later served as the CEO of both Home Lines and Hamburg Atlantic Line.[[2]](Home_Lines#cite_note-simplon-2)

## History

### Origins

Founded in <Genoa> in 1854 by Giacomo Costa (1836-1916) as Giacomo Costa fu Andrea, the company originally operated [cargo ships](Cargo_ship "Cargo ship"), carrying olive oils and textiles.[[5]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-:0-5) In 1924, the company was passed to the founder's sons (Federico, Eugenio and Enrico) and started commercial activities, buying the ship, *Ravenna*. In 1947, the name of the company was changed to Linea C.[[6]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-:6-6)

### Costa Line

In March 1948, passenger services were introduced,[[5]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-:0-5) beginning with regular services between Italy and [South America](South_America "South America") operated by the ship, *[Anna C](HMS_Southern_Prince "HMS Southern Prince").[[6]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-:6-6)* The ship departed from Genoa and reached Buenos Aires 16 days after departure. She marked the start of scheduled operations between Italy and South America after being the first [ocean liner](Ocean_liner "Ocean liner") to cross the South [Atlantic Ocean](Atlantic_Ocean "Atlantic Ocean") following [World War II](World_War_II "World War II").[[6]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-:6-6)

In 1958, Costa commissioned their first purpose-built ship, *[Federico C](SS_Federico_C. "SS Federico C.") ,* which provided a liner service between <Genoa>, Italy and [Buenos Aires](Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires"), Argentina via [Rio de Janeiro](Rio_de_Janeiro "Rio de Janeiro"), Brazil. In 1959, the company gradually transitioned into offering more pleasure holidays, with trips being offered in the [Mediterranean](Mediterranean_Sea "Mediterranean Sea") and the <Caribbean> regions.[[6]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-:6-6) The second purpose built ship, *[Eugenio C](SS_Eugenio_C "SS Eugenio C")*, debuted in 1966, designed by famous naval architect Nicolò Costanzi**.**[[7]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-7) Linea C went on to own 12 more ships by 1980, making the company the owner of the world's largest fleet of passenger ships.[[6]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-:6-6) In 1986, Linea C changed its name to Costa Cruises and became a cruise-centered business.[[6]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-:6-6)

The line had decided to modernize its fleet by the late 1980s, and ordered two new ships in 1987, which became *[Costa Classica](Margaritaville_at_Sea_Paradise "Margaritaville at Sea Paradise")* and *[Costa Romantica](Costa_neoRomantica "Costa neoRomantica")* entering service in 1991 and 1993 respectively. Costa wanted to create a new upscale European brand for their new ships and launched the short-lived EuroLuxe brand.[[8]](Costa_Cruises#cite_note-8)

**AIDA Cruises** is a German [cruise line](Cruise_line "Cruise line") founded in the early 1960s and organized as a wholly owned subsidiary of [Costa Crociere S.p.A.](Costa_Crociere_S.p.A. Based in [Rostock, Germany](Rostock "Rostock"),[[1]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-AidaHQ-1) AIDA Cruises caters primarily to the German-speaking market; as seagoing "club resorts", AIDA ships have on-board amenities and facilities designed to attract younger, more active vacationers.[[2]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-2) As of January 2023, the cruise line operates 12 ships.

AIDA Cruises has been Carnival-owned since 2003.[[3]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-smith160-3)[[4]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-:0-4)

## History

The company was founded in 1952 as [VEB](Volkseigener_Betrieb "Volkseigener Betrieb") Deutsche Seereederei Rostock (German Shipping Company Rostock) as the [German Democratic Republic](German_Democratic_Republic "German Democratic Republic")'s state-owned shipping company, based at <Rostock>, and became VEB Deutfracht/Seereederei Rostock in 1973.[[5]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-DSR-5) It began its passenger operations with *[Völkerfreundschaft](MS_Stockholm_(1948) "MS Stockholm (1948)")* ("Peoples' Friendship"), in the 1960.[[3]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-smith160-3) After the reunification of Germany in the early 1990s Deutfracht/Seereederei Rostock was privatised and became Deutsche Seereederei Rostock <GmbH>.[[5]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-DSR-5) DSR acquired Seetours of Bremen and cruises were marketed under the Seetours brand.[[3]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-smith160-3) On 1 January 1998, DSR split their operations into cargo and tourism, with a new company Arkona Touristik taking over the cruise business.[[6]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-nils-6) Then during 2000 a company was formed, known as AIDA Cruises; with [P&O Cruises](P%26O_Princess_Cruises "P&O Princess Cruises") acquiring a 51% stake in the new organisation, and Arkona Touristik retaining the other 49%.[[7]](AIDA_Cruises#cite_note-7)
